recognize_zh: A 圖骨髓中巨噬細胞內含大量粗大黃褐色含鐵血黃素顆粒（右下插圖），B 圖普魯士藍染色顯示鐵集中在巨噬細胞內呈深藍色；C 圖示意 hepcidin 使 ferroportin 被內化降解，說明發炎/自體免疫疾病時鐵被困在巨噬細胞內。
features: Bone marrow macrophages packed with coarse golden-brown refractile hemosiderin granules (panel A inset)
Background of erythroid and myeloid precursors with intervening fat spaces
Prussian blue stain shows heavy, clumped blue iron deposits confined to macrophages (panel B)
Increased storage iron in macrophages; ring sideroblasts not evident
Panel C is a schematic of hepcidin-induced ferroportin internalization in enterocytes and macrophages
describe_en: Bone marrow sections/aspirate show macrophages laden with coarse golden-brown hemosiderin pigment amid otherwise unremarkable hematopoietic precursors. An iron stain demonstrates markedly increased storage iron sequestered within macrophages, without evident ring sideroblasts in the illustrated field. The accompanying schematic depicts hepcidin binding ferroportin and triggering its lysosomal degradation, which blocks iron export from enterocytes and macrophages. In a patient with systemic autoimmune/inflammatory disease, findings are consistent with hepcidin-mediated macrophage iron sequestration (anemia of inflammation).

ddx.vs: Low hepcidin in HFE hemochromatosis causes parenchymal (hepatocyte) iron loading with relatively iron-poor macrophages, the opposite of this macrophage-predominant pattern.
Transfusional siderosis also loads macrophages but requires a history of multiple transfusions and shows markedly elevated ferritin with transferrin saturation often high.
Iron deficiency shows absent stainable marrow iron on Prussian blue, whereas storage iron is abundant here.
Ring sideroblasts show perinuclear iron granules within erythroblasts, not only macrophage iron as seen here.

stain: H&E or Giemsa; Prussian blue; schematic
